subject: botany
question_text: Describe the parts of a mature angiosperm embryo sac. Mention the role of synergids.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section (book p.19, LAQ 1). Botany holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. FIGURE SCOPE: the book prints a stippled oval with all cells; this card draws the simplified 7-celled, 8-nucleate Polygonum-type sac a student can reproduce — antipodals at the chalazal end, polar nuclei in the central cell, egg + synergids with filiform apparatus at the micropylar end.

page_header: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants · 8 marks

steps.label: The embryo sac
lines: The female gametophyte of angiosperms is
called the embryo sac.
The most common embryo sac is 7-celled and
8-nucleate — the Polygonum type.
It shows three main parts: the egg apparatus,
the antipodals and the central cell.
steps.why: The opening fixes the identity (embryo sac = female gametophyte), the standard organisation (7 cells, 8 nuclei, Polygonum type) and announces the three parts the rest of the answer will describe.
common_mistakes: Writing 8-celled. There are 8 NUCLEI but 7 cells — the central cell keeps two nuclei.
Calling the embryo sac the ovule. The sac lies INSIDE the ovule.
steps.memory_tip: 7 cells, 8 nuclei: 3 + 3 + 1 cells, and the 1 (central cell) holds 2 nuclei.
steps.margin_note: Three facts before the parts: female gametophyte, 7-celled 8-nucleate, Polygonum type.

steps.label: Diagram — mature embryo sac
steps.why: The positions ARE the physiology: the egg apparatus sits at the micropylar end because the pollen tube arrives through the micropyle; the antipodals sit at the far chalazal end. A drawing with the ends swapped is wrong even if every name is right.
common_mistakes: Placing the antipodals at the micropylar end. Antipodals are chalazal; the egg apparatus is micropylar.
Drawing one polar nucleus. There are two, in the central cell, before they fuse.
Leaving out the filiform apparatus at the synergid tips.
steps.memory_tip: Draw the oval, mark the two ends first, then fill: 3 antipodals at the chalazal end, 2 polar nuclei in the middle, egg + 2 synergids at the micropylar end.
steps.margin_note: Seven cells, both ends named, filiform apparatus shown — this is the 2-mark drawing.

steps.label: Egg apparatus
lines: Egg apparatus: a group of three cells at the
micropylar end of the embryo sac — one egg
cell and two synergids.
The synergids carry a filiform apparatus at
their micropylar tips.
steps.why: The egg apparatus is the business end of the sac: the egg is the female gamete, and the synergids beside it are the cells the pollen tube actually enters — so this part carries the most description marks.
common_mistakes: Writing two egg cells and one synergid — the ratio is 1 egg : 2 synergids.
Placing the egg apparatus at the chalazal end.
steps.memory_tip: At the door (micropyle): two helpers around one egg. Synergid means 'working together'.
steps.margin_note: Three cells, the end they occupy, and the filiform apparatus — all three facts for 2 marks.

steps.label: Antipodals
lines: Antipodals: three cells at the chalazal end
of the embryo sac.
They are the smallest, short-lived vegetative
cells, and they degenerate before or after
fertilisation.
steps.why: The antipodals balance the description: three cells at the opposite end, with no role in fertilisation — which is why they are called vegetative and why they degenerate.
common_mistakes: Giving the antipodals a role in fertilisation. They take no part and degenerate.
Writing two antipodals. Three antipodals mirror the three cells of the egg apparatus.
steps.memory_tip: ANTIpodal = at the opposite pole from the egg — three cells that fade away.
steps.margin_note: Position, count, 'vegetative', and their degeneration — four short facts.

steps.label: Central cell
lines: Central cell: the largest cell of the embryo
sac, containing two polar nuclei.
The polar nuclei often fuse at the centre to
form a single diploid secondary nucleus.
steps.why: The central cell matters for what comes later: its secondary nucleus (2n) is what the second male gamete joins in triple fusion to make the 3n endosperm.
common_mistakes: Calling the polar nuclei separate cells. They are two nuclei inside ONE cell.
Writing that the secondary nucleus is haploid — n + n makes it diploid.
steps.memory_tip: Biggest room, two nuclei: n + n → the 2n secondary nucleus waiting for triple fusion.
steps.margin_note: Largest cell, two polar nuclei, diploid secondary nucleus — the endosperm story starts here.

steps.label: Role of synergids

lines.text: Synergids absorb food and guide the tube

lines: They absorb nutrients from the nucellus.
Their filiform apparatus guides the entry of
the pollen tube into a synergid.
steps.why: The question asks this by name, so it gets its own step: nutrition (absorbing from the nucellus) and guidance (the filiform apparatus steering the pollen tube) are the two stated roles.
common_mistakes: Writing that the pollen tube enters the egg directly — it enters a SYNERGID through the filiform apparatus.
Giving only one of the two roles. Both absorption and guidance are expected.
steps.memory_tip: Synergids feed and lead: food from the nucellus in, pollen tube guided in.
steps.margin_note: A separately asked part — answer it under its own heading so the examiner finds it.

insider_note: 'Mention the role of synergids' is a named sub-question — leave it as its own labelled paragraph; burying it inside the egg-apparatus description is how this mark gets missed.
